lines: A bent tool can be reworked if the metal is worth saving. Show me you are.
Words are the handle. Actions hold everything together.
A poor strike can ruin good work. Learn control before you swing again.
Fine. Change the habit, not just the sentence.
I accept the apology. What you do next matters more.
Do not bring me another broken trust and ask why it failed.
Words start the repair. They do not finish it.
If you mean it, make the next choice better.
Thank you for saying it plainly.
That came out sharper than it should have. I am sorry too.
I hear you. I am not ready to forget it.
An apology does not erase the damage, but it gives us somewhere to start.
I will accept that. Give me time with the rest.
Say less now and prove more later.
You owned what you did. That counts for something.
I would rather have an honest apology than a clever excuse.
We can work forward from here if you keep your word.
I am still angry, but I believe you mean it.
That is enough for today. Do better tomorrow.
Alright. Let us see whether the repair holds.
